# Reference Notes 

Made By Abhik Biswas 

Prompt for subtopics: 

Act as an expert Curriculum Architect and GATE Physics Study Strategist. I have uploaded the official GATE syllabus as a document named “syllabus.pdf”. Locate and extract all topics listed under Section [INSERT SECTION NUMBER] within syllabus.pdf. 

A novice cannot study a flat list. Your task is to reorganize these exact topics into a “Cognitive Dependency Map.” You must reorder them strictly by logical, physical, and mathematical dependency—what must be mastered first to unlock the next concept. Furthermore, you must disintegrate each broad syllabus topic into its essential, bite-sized subtopics so a novice knows exactly what components to study. 

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS: 

1. ZERO CONVERSATIONAL FILLER. Start directly with the mapped output. Do not say “Here is the map.” 

2. Do not omit a single topic from the specified section of syllabus.pdf. Do not include topics from other sections. 

3. Classify the “Study Mode” for each topic using strictly one of these three tags: 

   - [Memory]: Pure facts, postulates, standard formulas, or definitions to memorize. 

   - [Deep Focus]: Requires intense, isolated mathematical and conceptual understanding of a single system. 

   - [Synthesis]: Highly complex; requires combining multiple previous topics to solve. 

Structure your output EXACTLY like this, grouping topics into logical Phases: 

## **Phase 1: [Name of the Foundation Phase]** 

1. [Exact Topic Name from Syllabus] 

- Subtopics: [Break this main topic down into a logical sequence of 3-5 core subtopics/concepts that must be studied step-by-step.] 

- The Link: [One sentence explaining why this topic must be learned right now, and what prior concept it builds upon.] 

- Study Mode: [Memory / Deep Focus / Synthesis] 

- Feeds Into: [Name the future syllabus topic that is impossible to understand without this.]
